interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Train Journey Begins: 5-Digit Numbers
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand how adding 1 to 9,999 creates 10,000, requiring the Ten Thousands (TTh) place value column.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Sanju and Mira look at the five-digit engine number and the town population signboard on the railway platform. In this interactive, students roll the unit wheels past 9,999 to watch all four digits reset to 0 and trigger the brand new 'Ten Thousands' dial to flip to 1, creating 10,000.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Students drag or click '+' on the odometer dials starting at 9,990. They can toggle between train engine numbers, odometer kilometre readings, and town census numbers up to 99,999.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: When 9,999 rolls to 10,000, a golden new column labelled 'TTh' lights up with a train whistle sound effect, displaying the expanded form: 10,000 = 1 Ten Thousand + 0 Th + 0 H + 0 T + 0 O.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Correctly assemble three target five-digit populations (e.g., 48,276) to earn 25 XP and the 'Odometer Engineer' micro-badge.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Place Value Architecture: The Ten Thousands
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Decompose multi-digit numbers into standard and expanded notation across TTh, Th, H, T, and O.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Mira explains that every digit's value depends on its column home. Students drag digit cards into a 5-column architectural chart to see how the digit 4 in 48,276 represents 40,000, while the digit 7 represents 70.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag digit tiles into columns. A slider expands and collapses between standard form (48,276) and expanded addition notation (40,000 + 8,000 + 200 + 70 + 6).
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Each column column illuminates in a distinctive color: Golden (TTh), Blue (Th), Green (H), Orange (T), Purple (O). Hovering shows multiplying factor (×10,000, ×1,000, etc.).
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Match expanded forms for 4 randomly generated 5-digit numbers without errors.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Token Model: Base-10 Manipulatives
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Physically experience the base-10 grouping rule: 10 of any unit bundle into 1 of the next higher unit.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Sanju uses yellow hundred-tokens, blue thousand-tokens, and golden ten-thousand tokens on the train table. Students bundle 10 loose hundred-tokens together and watch them fuse into a single blue thousand-token.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Students drag loose tokens into a bundling ring. Once 10 tokens enter the ring, an 'Exchange' button pulses. Clicking it replaces them with 1 higher-denomination token.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Particles swirl as 10 tokens morph with a satisfying chime into the higher token. A counter displays total monetary/numerical value continuously.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Represent 35,400 using the minimum number of physical tokens.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Number Line Estimations & The Jumping Rabbit
interactives.interactive_title: Hungry Rabbit Number Line Rounding Lab
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Develop spatial proximity intuition for rounding numbers to the nearest 10, 100, and 1,000.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: The hungry rabbit hops along the number line seeking the nearest carrot patch at multiples of 10, 100, or 1,000. At 48, the patch at 50 is visibly closer than 40. At 45 (the midpoint), the rabbit gathers energy and leaps forward to 50.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag the rabbit along a zoomable number line. Switch modes between 'Nearest 10', 'Nearest 100', and 'Nearest 1,000'. Release the rabbit to watch magnetic pulling forces drag it to the nearest benchmark.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Measurement calipers display exact distance from left and right benchmarks. Midpoints are highlighted with a glowing beacon indicating the 'round up' threshold.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Correctly place the rabbit on 5 challenging numbers and predict the rounded destination.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Mental Math, Puzzles & The Nim Game
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Apply symmetry and complement-pairing strategies in logical reasoning and problem solving.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: To pass the time on the long railway journey, Sanju and Mira play a traditional pebble game with two equal piles. Whoever takes the last pebble wins. Students discover that mirroring the first player's move guarantees victory.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Interactive piles of pebbles (e.g. 5 and 5). Players click on a pile and choose to remove 1, 2, or 3 pebbles. Play against the AI character 'Mira' or in two-player mode.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The board shows remaining pebble counts. A 'Symmetry Guide' toggle illuminates matching pairs in the opposite pile to illustrate winning strategies.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Defeat the AI by maintaining pile symmetry across 3 rounds.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Tamanna's Chocolates: Equal Sharing of Unequal Wholes
interactives.interactive_title: Chocolate Bar Equal Sharing & Balance Scale
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand that fractions are relative to the size of the whole; 1/3 of a large whole is greater than 1/3 of a small whole.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Tamanna and Kabir each have a chocolate bar of different lengths (300g vs 150g). Both take 1/3 of their bar. Students use a virtual cutting knife to divide each bar into 3 equal pieces, then place one slice of each on a pan balance to see why the 100g slice outbalances the 50g slice.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag cutter guide across two chocolate bars to make equal 3-part slices. Drag slices onto a dual pan balance.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Digital grams readout accompanies the tilt of the pan balance. Dynamic labels display: '1/3 of 300g = 100g' vs '1/3 of 150g = 50g'.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Prove why 1/3 is not always equal to another 1/3 when whole sizes differ.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Fraction Strips Wall
interactives.interactive_title: Dynamic Fraction Wall & Strip Comparison Tool
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Visually compare unit fractions and observe that as the denominator increases, the size of each part decreases.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Kabir aligns colorful paper strips divided into 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8 parts. Students drag horizontal marker lines across the wall to directly observe that 1/2 is longer than 1/3, which is longer than 1/4 and 1/8.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on any fraction strip to highlight it. Drag a vertical alignment laser line across multiple rows to compare strip lengths.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The highlighted strips glow in vibrant hues. An inequality statement (e.g., '1/2 > 1/4 > 1/8') updates automatically in real time.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Arrange 5 fractions in ascending order by dragging strips onto a comparison track.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Equivalent Fractions: Same Value, Different Names
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Generate and verify equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by common factors.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Tamanna shades half of a circular roti or grid. Students slide a 'Subdivision' control from 2 parts to 4, 6, and 8 parts, observing that while the piece count multiplies, the total shaded yellow area remains identical.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Shade sectors of a circle or rectangle. Use a slider to split each section into 2, 3, or 4 sub-pieces.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Live equation displays: 1/2 = (1×2)/(2×2) = 2/4 = (1×4)/(2×4) = 4/8. Shaded area percentage displays 50% continuously.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Find 3 different equivalent forms for 2/3 and 3/4.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Fractions of Collections & Real-World Problems
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Calculate fractions of discrete quantities (e.g. 1/4 of 24 apples = 6 apples).
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Kabir and Tamanna have 24 apples in a basket to share with neighbours. Students drag apples equally into 4 recipient trays, discovering that 1/4 of the collection of 24 is exactly 6 apples.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag apples into partitioned plates or click 'Equal Share'. Adjust total collection size (12, 18, 24, 30) and fraction divisor.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Trays update with count labels: 'Tray 1: 6 apples (1/4)'. An operation breakdown pops up: '24 ÷ 4 = 6'.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Solve 3 sharing challenges involving fractions of collections.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Statue Game: Full, Half, and Quarter Turns
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Recognize that angles measure the amount of turning from a starting direction.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Students play the classroom 'Statue' game. A dancing avatar rotates on screen until the teacher shouts 'Statue!'. Students identify whether the rotation was a quarter turn (90°), half turn (180°), or full turn (360°).
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Rotate a steering dial or click 'Quarter Turn', 'Half Turn', 'Three-Quarter Turn'. Watch the dancer face North, East, South, or West.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: An arc sweeps out the angle with degrees and fraction of full turn (1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1). A chime plays upon completing clean quarter turns.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Stop the dancer precisely at 3 target directions called out by the teacher.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Angle Tester & The Right Angle
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Use an L-shaped angle tester to test whether corners of classroom objects form exact right angles (90°).
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Rohini constructs an angle tester using two cardboard strips joined by a brass pin. In this interactive, students drag the virtual cardboard tester to corners of book covers, doors, scissors, and window panes to verify if they form a perfect 'L' right angle.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag the cardboard arms to widen or narrow the tester. Snap the corner of the tester onto various classroom objects.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: If the object corner fits snugly, the tester glows green: 'Perfect Right Angle (90°)!'. If narrower, it glows yellow ('Acute'); if wider, it glows orange ('Obtuse').
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Test and identify 5 right angles in the virtual classroom room.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Acute & Obtuse Angles on Clock Hands
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Classify angles as acute (< 90°), right (= 90°), or obtuse (> 90°) using analog clock hand positions.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Mohini observes that at 3:00 and 9:00, clock hands form right angles, while at 2:00 they make an acute angle, and at 5:00 they make an obtuse angle. Students drag clock hands to any time to see the angle classified instantly.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag minute and hour hands smoothly around an analog clock dial.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The pie wedge between the hands changes color dynamically: Green for Right (90°), Blue for Acute (e.g. 60° at 2:00), Red for Obtuse (e.g. 150° at 5:00). Exact degree readout displays alongside.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Set the clock to create 2 different acute angles, 2 right angles, and 2 obtuse angles.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Equal Sum Groups: Interchanging Pairs
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Apply mental addition and difference-halving strategies to balance group sums.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Students look at two groups of numbers whose sums are unequal. By swapping one tile from Group A with one tile from Group B whose difference equals half the total sum difference, both groups achieve perfect sum equality.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag number tiles between Pan A and Pan B. Watch the scale beam tilt according to the weight/sum of each side.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The scale beam tilts dynamically. Live sum badges display: 'Sum A = 54', 'Sum B = 46', 'Difference = 8'. When balanced at 50 each, the beam levels out with golden sparkles.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Balance 3 different number sets by swapping single pairs.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Travel Milestone Map: Distance Calculations
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Solve multi-step distance word problems using collinear milestone positions.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Mira views milestone markers along national highways. A milestone shows 185 km to Delhi and 260 km in the opposite direction to Jaipur. Students drive a car along the line to calculate total segment distances.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Slide the car along the highway line. Place milestones at custom positions to test distance subtraction and addition.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Distance brackets highlight the two legs. An animated equation bar computes: 185 km + 260 km = 445 km total distance.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Calculate total journeys across 3 multi-city itineraries.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Magic Hexagons: Computational Patterns
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Solve relational multiplication and division constraints in geometric configurations.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Sanju discovers a magic hexagon where each square between two corner circles equals their product. Students fill in missing numbers using forward multiplication and backward division.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on empty circle and square nodes in a hexagon graph. Type numbers or select from a palette.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Lines connecting nodes pulse green when the product relation (A × B = Square) is satisfied, or red when mismatched.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Complete 2 magic hexagons with all 6 edges verified.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Choosing the Appropriate Unit: mm, cm, m, and km
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Select appropriate metric units (mm, cm, m, km) based on real-world magnitude.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Cheenu and Deepu realize an ant's leg cannot be measured in metres, nor a road trip in millimetres. Students drag various everyday items into the correct metric unit basket.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag items (grain of rice, textbook, blackboard, marathon road) into mm, cm, m, or km sorting bins.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A zoomable powers-of-10 universe slider shows where each item lives from 1 mm up to 1,000,000 mm (1 km).
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Correctly categorize 8 items across the 4 metric units.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Precision Ruler Readings & Decimals
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Read decimal subdivisions of centimetres as millimetres (e.g. 6 cm and 4 mm = 6.4 cm).
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Deepu measures a crayon that falls between 6 cm and 7 cm. Using a magnifying glass, students count the 4 small millimetre tick marks to record the measurement as 6.4 cm.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag objects against a virtual wooden ruler. Drag a magnifying loupe over the end of the object to see tiny mm subdivisions clearly.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The loupe shows an expanded view with tick marks 0.1 through 0.9 cm highlighted. A digital readout updates: '6 cm + 4 mm = 6.4 cm'.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Measure 4 objects with sub-millimetre precision.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Map Scales: Centimetres on Paper to Kilometres on Ground
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Translate ratio scales (e.g. 1 cm = 100 km) into real-world geographical distances.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Cheenu measures distance between two cities on a state map. The ruler shows 3.5 cm. With a scale of 1 cm = 100 km, students discover that the actual ground distance is 350 km.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on any two cities on an India map. A digital ruler stretches between them. Adjust the scale ratio slider (1 cm = 50 km, 100 km, 200 km).
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A conversion card calculates: Map Distance (3.5 cm) × Scale (100 km/cm) = 350 km Ground Distance.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Calculate distances for 3 real city routes on the map.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Dairy Mystery: Shape Equations
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Use number clues and substitution to discover secret numbers between 1 and 24 hidden behind shapes.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: At the village dairy, Gopal sets up puzzles where shapes stand for secret numbers. If Triangle + Triangle = Circle, and Circle × Triangle = 16, students deduce that Triangle = 2 and Circle = 4.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on shape slots and input deduced numbers. A balance equation checker tests if all simultaneous equations hold true.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Satisfied equations glow emerald green. Contradictory guesses trigger a hint indicating which relation failed.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Crack 3 dairy shape puzzles to unlock the 'Dairy Detective' badge.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Milk Pouch Packing Arrays
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Find all factor pairs for a given composite number by constructing rectangular grids.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Ananya packs 24 buttermilk pouches into delivery crates. Students reshape the crate grid into 1×24, 2×12, 3×8, and 4×6, proving that 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24 are all factors of 24.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag grid corner handles to resize crate rows and columns until the total pouch count matches the target number (e.g. 24 or 36).
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A factors catalog fills up on the side: '✓ Found: 3 rows of 8 = 24'. Total factor count updates in real time.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Discover all 8 factor arrangements for 24 pouches.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Factor Trees & Prime Factorization
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Decompose composite numbers into prime building blocks through hierarchical tree branching.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Gopal compares numbers to trees. Students take 36 and branch it into 6 × 6, then branch each 6 into 2 × 3. They observe that even if they start with 4 × 9, the final leaf primes are always 2, 2, 3, 3.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on any composite node in a factor tree to split it into two factor branches. Type or pick factors.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Prime numbers (2, 3, 5, 7) turn into golden leaves that cannot be split further. A synthesis statement forms at the bottom: 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Fully factorize 3 numbers into prime leaves.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Traditional Woven Basket & Mat Patterns
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand how repeating mathematical interlacing rules (over-2, under-2) generate complex visual patterns.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: An elder weaver shows Tara how interlacing bamboo strips creates stepped diagonal zigzags. In this simulator, students toggle interlacing rules across warp and weft threads to watch geometric textures emerge.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click grid intersections or set algorithmic rules (e.g. 'Over 1, Under 1' or 'Over 2, Under 2, Shift 1'). Change thread colors.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The woven mat renders with realistic 3D shadow depths, showing threads passing over and under in authentic bamboo style.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Recreate the traditional chevron zigzag pattern.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Floor Tessellations: Tiling Without Gaps
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Prove that regular polygons tessellate if and only if their interior angles around each vertex sum to exactly 360°.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Tara tries to tile floor mats with regular pentagons and finds awkward gaps. Students drag regular polygons (triangles 60°, squares 90°, hexagons 120°, pentagons 108°) around a central vertex to see why three hexagons (3 × 120° = 360°) tile perfectly while pentagons leave gaps.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag polygons from a tray to snap around a central vertex point.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A circular angle dial shows sum around the vertex: '3 × 120° = 360° (PERFECT TILE!)' vs '3 × 108° = 324° (GAP OF 36°!)'.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Discover the 3 regular tessellations (triangles, squares, hexagons).

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Symmetry Grids & Repeating Motifs
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Apply two-fold reflection across horizontal and vertical axes to produce symmetrical motifs.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Tara draws a motif on the top-left quadrant of a square mat. As she colors individual cells, the computer mirrors them automatically across vertical and horizontal center lines to produce an intricate royal carpet design.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Paint cells on an 8×8 or 16×16 grid quadrant using a color palette. Toggle vertical, horizontal, and diagonal mirror axes.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: All 4 quadrants update simultaneously in real time. Download or print the completed symmetrical mat design.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Design a symmetrical carpet motif with at least 2 axes of reflection.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Anu's Estimation Checklist: Grams vs. Kilograms
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Develop realistic benchmarks for mass: grams for lightweight items, kilograms for heavy items.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Anu corrects an absurd household checklist that claimed an iron almirah weighs 40 grams. Students match realistic weight tags (40 g, 400 g, 4 kg, 40 kg, 400 kg) to household objects.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag weight labels to furniture, groceries, and stationery items. Click 'Check Estimates' to verify.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Correct placements lock in with a cheerful ring. Ridiculous mismatches trigger comical visual animations (e.g. an ant trying to lift an almirah marked 40g).
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Correctly estimate weights for 6 household items without mistakes.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Pan Balance: Balancing Weights
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Solve mass equivalence problems using pan balances (e.g. 1 kg = 2 × 500 g = 4 × 250 g).
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Mother asks Anu to balance 1 kg on the left pan. Students select combinations of 500g, 250g, 100g, and 50g brass weights to place on the right pan until the balance beam reaches perfect horizontal equilibrium.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag standard brass weights onto right pan. Watch balance needle move toward center zero mark.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The balance beam tilts with realistic physics. A balance needle indicates 'Heavy Left', 'Balanced', or 'Heavy Right'. Total grams computed in real time.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Balance 2 kg using at least 4 different weight denominations.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Liquid Capacity: Millilitres and Litres
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand capacity conversions: 1 Litre = 1,000 Millilitres, and calculate glass fills.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Anu compares a 5 mL cough syrup spoon with a 200 mL drinking glass and a 1 L water bottle. Students pour 200 mL glasses of water into the bottle, observing that exactly 5 glasses fill the 1,000 mL volume.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click to pour from measuring cups (50 mL, 100 mL, 200 mL, 250 mL) into a 1-litre graduated cylinder.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Water level rises with realistic liquid sound and splash animation. Graduated markings highlight 200, 400, 600, 800, and 1,000 mL milestones.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Fill exactly 1,000 mL without overflowing using the fewest pours.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Coconut Array: Multiplication & Division Twins
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Recognize that every multiplication fact gives rise to two twin division facts (5 × 7 = 35 ➔ 35 ÷ 7 = 5 and 35 ÷ 5 = 7).
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: A roadside vendor stacks 35 coconuts in an orderly grid. Students drag horizontal or vertical partition ropes across the coconuts to split them into 7 groups of 5, or 5 groups of 7, discovering the reciprocal nature of division.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag splitting ropes to group 35 coconuts vertically or horizontally.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Equation cards update dynamically: '7 rows × 5 coconuts = 35 coconuts' and '35 ÷ 7 = 5'.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Formulate both division facts for 3 different rectangular coconut arrays.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Dividend, Divisor, and Quotient: Fact Family Houses
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Master standard division terminology: Dividend (N), Divisor (D), Quotient (Q).
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Aditi builds fact family houses. The roof shows the product (Dividend N = 48), while the two lower windows show the factors (Divisor D = 6, Quotient Q = 8). Students arrange tiles into their proper architectural homes.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag number tiles into the Roof (Dividend), Left Window (Divisor), and Right Window (Quotient).
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The house lights up and displays all 4 related equations (A × B = C, B × A = C, C ÷ A = B, C ÷ B = A).
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Construct 3 complete fact family houses.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Equal Grouping, Packaging & Word Problems
interactives.interactive_title: Sweet Box Packaging Machine with Remainder Tray
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Model division with remainders: Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: The sweet shop needs to pack 50 laddoo boxes into shipping cartons that hold 6 boxes each. Students run a virtual packaging machine that packs 8 full cartons (48 boxes) and diverts the 2 remaining boxes into a leftover tray.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Set total items (e.g. 50) and carton capacity (e.g. 6). Press 'Pack Carton'.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Cartons fill and seal with a stamp: 'Carton 1..8 Full!'. Leftover tray catches 2 boxes. Equation updates: 50 ÷ 6 = 8 R 2 (50 = 6 × 8 + 2).
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Solve 3 packaging scenarios with non-zero remainders.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Birthday Cutouts: Lines of Symmetry
interactives.interactive_title: Paper Fold & Snip Alphabet Symmetry Studio
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Identify reflectional line symmetry and construct symmetrical shapes through single-fold cutouts.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Prem and Manu make 'Happy Birthday' cutouts. Prem shows that folding paper vertically means only cutting half the letter 'A' or 'M'. In this simulator, students fold paper, draw on one half, and unfold to reveal the full symmetrical letter.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Fold virtual paper along a dashed center crease. Draw cutting paths on one side using a virtual scissor. Click 'Unfold'.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The paper unfolds smoothly in 3D animation, revealing the completed symmetrical cutout. The central crease glows as the 'Line of Symmetry'.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Successfully cut out letters 'A', 'M', and 'T' using single folds.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Horizontal vs. Vertical Lines of Symmetry
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Distinguish between vertical, horizontal, dual, and non-symmetrical alphabet letters.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Manu finds that 'H' has both vertical and horizontal symmetry, while 'B' has only horizontal, 'M' has only vertical, and 'F' has none. Students sort all 26 capital letters into a 4-quadrant Venn diagram.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag letters from an alphabet tray into 4 Venn zones: 'Vertical Only', 'Horizontal Only', 'Both Axes', 'No Line Symmetry'.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Dropping a letter triggers folding lines that test each axis automatically with green checkmarks or red X's.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Correctly sort 10 selected letters into their symmetry categories.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Mirror Reflections & Symmetrical Patterns
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand that an object and its mirror image are congruent and equidistant from the reflection line.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Prem places a pocket mirror along dashed lines on geometric drawings. Students slide a virtual mirror tool across split illustrations to complete butterfly wings, rangoli patterns, and decorative masks.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag and rotate a virtual mirror blade across a canvas. Change the reflection axis angle.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The mirror glass renders a real-time virtual reflection of the half-shape, completing the full figure seamlessly when placed on the true line of symmetry.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Locate the exact mirror line for 4 complex rangoli designs.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Decorating the Quilt Border: Perimeter
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Calculate perimeter as the total distance around a closed 2D boundary: Perimeter = 2 × (Length + Width).
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Preetha and Grandmother stitch lace around a quilt measuring 2m by 1.5m. Students drag a virtual measuring ribbon around all four edges, unrolling the ribbon into a straight line to measure the total 7m boundary.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click each edge of rectangular and irregular quilt patches to trace golden border lace. Watch the tape unroll on a linear scale.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Each edge adds to a running sum: 2m + 1.5m + 2m + 1.5m = 7 metres. The lace shimmers when the loop closes.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Calculate lace required for 3 quilts of varying dimensions.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Grid Area: Counting 1 cm² Squares
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Measure 2D area by counting whole and half unit squares on a transparent centimetre grid.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Adrit places a transparent 1 cm square grid over irregularly shaped quilt patches. Students count full squares inside the boundary and combine two half-squares into full units to calculate total surface area.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on grid squares inside a shape to count them. Toggle 'Half-Square Combiner' to merge triangular fragments.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Full squares glow green (1 cm² each), half squares glow amber (0.5 cm²). A live tally calculates: Full (10) + Halves (4) = 12 cm².
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Accurately compute the area of 3 complex patch shapes.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Different Shapes, Same Area
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Prove that shapes with the exact same area can have dramatically different perimeters.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Adrit discovers that a 1×12 rectangle and a 3×4 rectangle both cover 12 cm², yet the long skinny one needs 26 cm of border lace while the compact one needs only 14 cm. Students reshape 12 square blocks into various configurations.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Rearrange 12 unit square blocks into different connected polyomino shapes.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A comparative dashboard displays Area (fixed at 12 cm²) vs Perimeter (ranging from 14 cm to 26 cm) with real-time border highlighting.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Construct the shape with maximum perimeter and minimum perimeter for 12 unit squares.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Raghav's Morning Yoga: Reading Clock Times
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Calculate elapsed time duration by subtracting start time from finish time.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Raghav starts his yoga asanas at 6:15 AM and finishes at 6:40 AM. Students drag clock hands to set start and end times, watching the elapsed wedge highlight 25 minutes of mindfulness.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Set start and finish times on dual side-by-side clocks. Drag the timeline scrub bar.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A timeline ribbon fills between the two times. A step-by-step subtraction readout confirms: 6:40 AM - 6:15 AM = 25 minutes.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Calculate correct activity durations across 3 daily school routines.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Stopwatch: Racing Seconds
interactives.interactive_title: Digital Sprint Stopwatch & Split Lap Timer
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Measure small time intervals in seconds and tenths of seconds.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: The PT Teacher uses a digital stopwatch to time Raghav's 100m sprint. Students trigger a stopwatch as runners sprint across a digital track, recording split seconds and comparing finishing order.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click 'Start / Split / Stop' buttons on a high-precision digital stopwatch interface.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Runners animate along lanes; clicking 'Split' logs exact times: Runner A = 14.8 s, Runner B = 15.2 s. Difference (0.4 s) highlighted.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Time 3 race events and rank runners by fastest duration.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Daily Timelines & 24-Hour Railway Clocks
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Seamlessly convert between 12-hour AM/PM civil time and 24-hour railway time.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Raghav checks his train ticket showing departure at 17:30. Students drag a 24-hour solar dial from midnight (00:00) through morning (08:00 AM) to afternoon (17:30 = 5:30 PM), understanding why 12 is added after noon.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Rotate a single master slider representing 24 hours of the day. Watch sunrise, noon, sunset, and midnight cycle.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Dual digital clocks update in tandem: Standard (5:30 PM) and Railway (17:30). A visual helper highlights the '+12' conversion rule for PM hours.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Correctly convert 5 train timetable departure times.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Mystery Multiplier Box: Input-Output Machines
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Deduce algebraic multiplication function rules by observing paired inputs and outputs.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Freddy Frog drops numbers into a mystery wooden box. When 3 goes in, 18 comes out; when 5 goes in, 30 comes out. Students drop various test numbers into the funnel to discover that the box multiplies every input by 6.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag input number balls (2, 4, 7, 9) into the top funnel of the machine. Watch the gear mechanism spin and spit out the transformed number.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A table logs: Input | Output | Output ÷ Input. A keypad asks: 'What is the secret multiplier?'. Correct guess opens the machine.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Crack 3 mystery multiplier machines with different scaling factors.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Animal Jumps on the Number Line
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Generate sequences of multiples through skip counting on an extended number line.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Ruby Rabbit hops in 3s (0, 3, 6, 9, 12...) while Freddy Frog hops in 2s (0, 2, 4, 6, 8...). Students trigger animal jumps along a number line track to visualize sequences of multiples as repeated equal distances.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Select animal (Frog = 2, Rabbit = 3, Kangaroo = 5). Click 'Hop' to watch them leap forward along the line.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Each leap leaves glowing colored footprint stamps on numbers. A multiples strip records the mathematical sequence.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Complete 10 hops for each animal without missing any multiples.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Common Multiples & The Meeting Spot
interactives.interactive_title: Least Common Multiple (LCM) Meeting Spot Locator
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Find common multiples and the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of two or three numbers.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Freddy (hops 2), Ruby (hops 3), and Koko Kangaroo (hops 5) jump simultaneously along the line. Students identify the stepping stones where their footprints overlap, discovering that 30 is their very first shared landing spot (LCM).
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Animate all 3 animals jumping together along a number line from 0 to 60. Click on stones with multiple footprint overlays.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: When animals land together on step 30 and 60, confetti shoots up and a fanfare plays: 'LCM Found! LCM(2, 3, 5) = 30'.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Find the LCM for (3, 4), (4, 6), and (2, 3, 5).

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Facing the Rising Sun: Cardinal Directions
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Deduce North, South, East, and West using the position of the rising Sun.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Manu stands outside at dawn facing the rising Sun. By facing East, his back is West, his left arm points North, and his right arm points South. Students rotate Manu to learn cardinal direction relationships.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Rotate Manu's avatar 360 degrees using a compass dial. Observe the Sun rising in the East and setting in the West.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Dynamic direction arrows point from Manu's arms, chest, and back. Compass rose updates synchronously with cardinal and ordinal headings.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Orient Manu correctly to face North, East, South, and West upon command.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: The Four Little Chicks Direction Puzzle
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Navigate 2D grid coordinates using cardinal directions and relative turns.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Four little chicks are lost on a farm grid. Chick 1 walks 3 steps North then turns East; Chick 2 walks 2 steps West then turns South. Students program movement vectors to guide all chicks back to the mother hen.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Program directional commands (North, South, East, West + step count) for each chick.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Chicks waddle step-by-step leaving colored trail lines on the grid. A collision detection engine alerts if obstacles are encountered.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Guide all 4 chicks safely to the coop in the minimum number of steps.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Grid Maps: Navigating the Neighborhood
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Read map legends, grid references, and plan optimal routes between urban landmarks.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Manu reads a grid map of his neighborhood. The school is at grid B3, the park at D5, and the hospital at A2. Students plan routes using cardinal directions while avoiding roadblocks.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on map grid intersections to trace a route from Home to School. Check landmark descriptions in the map legend.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A route itinerary logs step-by-step instructions: 'Walk 2 blocks North on Park Road, turn East onto Main Street for 3 blocks'. Total distance calculated.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Find the shortest route between 3 landmark pairs.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Child TV Reporters: Collecting Survey Data
interactives.interactive_title: Child TV Reporter Live Peer Survey Station
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Collect and log statistical survey data systematically using standardized categories.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Samaira and Kabir act as roving reporters interviewing students about how many hours they watch TV and their favorite programs (Cartoons, Sports, News, Music). Students interview virtual peers and record responses.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on student avatars in a schoolyard to ask their preferences. Drag response cards into raw data bins.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Avatars answer with speech bubbles: 'I love Sports! I play cricket 2 hours a day!'. Response counters increment in real time.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Complete a 20-student classroom survey.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Tally Marks & Frequency Tables
interactives.interactive_title: Five-Bar Gate Tally Mark Frequency Organizer
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Group statistical counts using 5-bar tally marks (卌) and compile frequency tables.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Kabir organizes raw survey data into bunches of 5 using tally marks. Students click to add vertical strokes, watching the 5th stroke cross diagonally to form a neat bundle of 5.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click '+ Tally' for each survey item. The 5th click automatically draws a diagonal crossbar to lock the bundle.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Tally glyphs render authentically. A frequency column automatically calculates totals: 3 bundles + 2 single strokes = 17.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Organize 4 survey categories into a flawless frequency table.

interactives.subject: Mathematics
interactives.lesson_title: Pictographs and Bar Charts
interactives.interactive_title: Dynamic Pictograph & Vertical Bar Chart Studio
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Construct, scale, and interpret pictographs and vertical bar graphs.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Samaira presents survey findings on a colorful bar chart. Students adjust the scale key (1 icon = 2 students vs 1 icon = 5 students), drag bar heights, and interpret which program is most popular.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag vertical bar heights to match frequency values. Switch between 'Pictograph Mode' and 'Bar Chart Mode'. Change y-axis scale increments.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Bars animate up with smooth transitions and hover tooltips showing exact values. Grid lines highlight benchmarks.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Create a bar chart that accurately reflects the TV survey data.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Rain at the Window: Observing Water Everywhere
interactives.interactive_title: Global Blue Planet 3D Water & Land Ratio Explorer
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand that water covers over 70% of Earth's surface and is essential for all living organisms.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Afreen and Jyoti watch raindrops on their window and wonder how much of Earth is covered by water. Students rotate a 3D Earth globe, toggle ocean and land layers, and discover that over 71% of Earth's surface is blue water.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Rotate a 3D Earth sphere. Drag a percentage slider to drain or fill ocean basins to visualize the 71% water to 29% land ratio.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A pie chart updates in real time showing oceanic vs freshwater vs land proportions. Continents and major ocean trenches highlight on hover.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Identify the 5 major oceans and measure Earth's total water coverage.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: States of Matter & The Condensation Mystery
interactives.interactive_title: Ice Tumbler Condensation & States of Matter Lab
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Demonstrate that atmospheric water vapour condenses into liquid droplets upon touching cold surfaces.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Afreen places ice cubes inside a dry steel glass. Outside droplets appear. In this simulation, students adjust glass temperature from 30°C down to 0°C, watching invisible surrounding air molecules cool and condense into glittering droplets on the exterior metal surface.

interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Microscopic view reveals invisible gas particles slowing down upon contacting the cold glass and coalescing into liquid water beads that run down the side.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Prove that the droplets come from surrounding air and not from glass leakage.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: The Complete Water Cycle
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Trace the continuous closed cycle of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Students control the global water cycle. By increasing solar heat, ocean water evaporates into vapour; cooling upper air condenses vapour into fluffy cumulus clouds; saturating clouds precipitates rain and snow over mountains, flowing back to rivers.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag the 'Sun Intensity' slider. Click on clouds to trigger rainfall. Track individual water droplet journeys from ocean to cloud to river.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Arrows animate along all 4 cycle phases. A droplet tracker highlights the perpetual closed thermodynamic loop with zero net water loss.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Successfully complete 2 full cycles of water from ocean evaporation to river return.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Soil Water Percolation & Groundwater Recharge
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Observe how permeable topsoil allows rainwater percolation to recharge underground aquifers, while impermeable surfaces cause runoff.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Jyoti pours water on garden soil and watches it soak in, while on concrete it puddles and runs away. Students pour rain onto 3 soil columns (Garden Loam, Sand, Concrete) to observe percolation rates and well replenishment.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Pour equal volumes of water over soil columns. Measure percolation time with a stopwatch and observe underground water table rise.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Cross-section view shows water filtering through soil layers into an aquifer. Concrete column triggers flash flooding; loam column recharges a village well.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Explain why urban green cover is essential for preventing city floods and recharging wells.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: India's Major Rivers & Wetland Conservation
interactives.interactive_title: Interactive River Basins & Wetland Ecosystem Map
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Map major river basins of India and understand wetland biodiversity and water conservation.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Afreen studies a physical map of Indian river systems: Ganga, Brahmaputra, Godavari, Krishna, Narmada. Students click on river basins to follow their courses and inspect wetland ecosystems supporting lotus leaves, fish, and migratory birds.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on major river origins to trace flow lines across states. Inspect wetland wildlife cards.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Rivers illuminate in blue ribbons flowing toward the Arabian Sea or Bay of Bengal. Elevation profiles show mountain descents.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Trace 4 major Indian river systems from source to sea.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Where I Begin: Origin in the Western Ghats
interactives.interactive_title: River Godavari Headwaters & Watershed Origin Lab
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Identify mountain origins of peninsular rivers at Trimbakeshwar and understand watershed runoff.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: River Godavari narrates her birth in the lush Western Ghats of Maharashtra. Students explore how monsoon rainfall on high basalt ridges gathers into mountain rills and waterfalls, combining to birth a mighty river.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Simulate rainfall over the Western Ghats mountain ridges. Watch rills merge into cascading streams.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Streamflow meter tracks volume (cubic metres/second) as tributaries join the parent river trunk.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Track Godavari's first 50 kilometres through the Western Ghats.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: River Ecosystem: Flora, Fauna, and Aquatic Life
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Analyze aquatic ecosystems, dissolved oxygen levels, and food web dependencies.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Fisherman Kaka shows how clean river waters support diverse life: algae, aquatic insects, mahseer fish, otters, and diving kingfishers. Students connect species in a balanced food chain.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag organisms into their trophic niches (Producer, Primary Consumer, Secondary Consumer, Apex Predator).
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Healthy energy flow arrows connect organisms. An oxygen meter shows 8 mg/L dissolved O2 supporting abundant fish life.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Build a sustainable 4-tier freshwater food web.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Human Settlements, Farms & Pollution
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Evaluate anthropogenic river pollution and understand wastewater treatment operations.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: As Godavari flows past major towns, untreated domestic sewage and agricultural chemicals pollute her waters. Students install Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) stages (Screening, Aeration, Settling) to clean effluents before river discharge.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Activate STP treatment stages. Toggle industrial and municipal pipe discharges to observe river water clarity and dissolved oxygen.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: River water changes from murky brown to clear blue. Dissolved oxygen rises, bringing back fish schools.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Restore river water quality from 'Severely Polluted' to 'Bathing & Aquatic Grade'.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: The Delta & Merging with the Ocean
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Model river delta formation, sediment deposition, and brackish mangrove estuaries.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Near the Bay of Bengal, Godavari slows down and splits into distributary branches, depositing nutrient-rich silt to create a fertile delta. Students adjust river velocity to observe silt deposition patterns.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Adjust river speed and sediment load sliders. Observe fan-shaped delta growth at the coastline.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Sediment particles settle as flow slows down, creating distributary islands and mangrove channels teeming with mudskippers and crabs.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Form a stable delta network with at least 3 distributary channels.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: The Balanced Thali: Nutrients Our Body Needs
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Identify food groups (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, roughage) and assemble a balanced diet.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Dr. Anita reviews the traditional Indian thali. Students choose food items (roti, dal, leafy vegetables, curd, seasonal fruit) to balance an interactive nutrient dashboard.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag food bowls onto a brass thali plate. Watch carbohydrate, protein, fat, and vitamin gauges fill.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Nutrient gauges indicate 'Under / Balanced / Excess'. When all 5 essential nutrient categories reach optimal levels, the plate glows with a 'Balanced Thali' seal.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Construct a balanced meal plate meeting 100% daily nutritional guidelines.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: From Tasting to Digesting
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Trace the pathway of food through mouth mastication, salivary starch breakdown, stomach churning, and small intestine absorption.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Rohan chews a piece of dry chapati for 30 seconds and notices it turns sweet as saliva breaks down complex starches. Students navigate a bite of food down the esophagus, through stomach acid, into the nutrient-absorbing villi of the small intestine.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click to chew, release salivary enzymes, churn stomach muscles, and absorb nutrients through intestinal villi.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Molecular animations show starches turning to glucose. Organs illuminate along the 9-metre gastrointestinal tract.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Guide a meal through all 4 stages of digestion and absorption.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Seasonal Agriculture: Millets and Grains
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Recognize the environmental and nutritional advantages of traditional millets (Ragi, Jowar, Bajra).
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Dadi explains that millets grow with very little water and enrich the soil naturally. Students test crop resilience by subjecting wheat, rice, and millets to drought conditions, observing that millets stay vibrant with 70% less irrigation.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Adjust rainfall and temperature sliders across different farm plots growing rice, wheat, and bajra/ragi.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Water usage gauges compare irrigation needs (Rice needs 1,200mm vs Bajra needs 350mm). Soil health indicators update.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Grow a successful drought-tolerant harvest of nutrient-rich millets.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Traditional Food Preservation Techniques
interactives.interactive_title: Traditional Food Preservation & Spoilage Prevention Lab
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand how removing moisture (drying) or creating high osmotic barriers (salting, pickling) prevents microbial spoilage.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Dadi prepares raw mango pickle. Students explore how salt draws moisture out of fruit slices through osmosis, and how oil forms an airtight barrier preventing fungal spores from germinating.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Choose preservation treatment (Sun-Drying, Salting, Pickling in Oil, Refrigeration) for raw mangoes, peas, and fish.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A shelf-life clock advances by months. Microbe counters show zero bacterial growth in properly preserved jars.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Preserve 3 seasonal foods to last through winter without spoilage.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Aasha and Mohit's Vision: What Makes a School Green?
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Identify environmental improvements that transform a conventional school into an eco-friendly campus.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Aasha and Mohit envision their school with shade trees, solar panels, rainwater harvesting, and clean air. Students drag sustainable infrastructure onto a school blueprint to raise its Eco-Score.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Place green features (solar rooftop, rainwater filter, compost pit, native hedge) onto an architectural school map.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Campus Eco-Score increases from 20% to 100%. Carbon footprint and electricity bill counters decrease visibly.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Upgrade the campus to earn five green leaves accreditation.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Waste Segregation & The Compost Pit
interactives.interactive_title: Waste Segregation Sorter & Aerobic Compost Pit
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Segregate wet biodegradable waste from dry recyclables and track decomposition in a compost pit.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Mohit sets up Green (wet organic) and Blue (dry recyclable) bins. Students sort fruit peels, plastic wrappers, cardboard, and fallen leaves. Wet waste goes to the compost pit, where aerobic microbes turn it into black compost.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag trash items from school lunchboxes into Green or Blue bins. Turn the compost pile with a virtual pitchfork.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Compost pit temperature rises to 55°C (indicating healthy microbial decomposition). After 4 virtual weeks, waste turns into rich potting soil.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Sort 15 waste items with 100% accuracy and harvest finished compost.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: School Herbal Gardens & Habitat for Birds
interactives.interactive_title: School Biodiversity & Bird Oasis Habitat Creator
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Create microhabitats for urban birds and pollinators using native plants and clay water bowls.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Aasha plants Tulsi, Mint, and marigolds in the schoolyard and sets up a shallow clay bird bath. Students maintain water levels and watch sparrows, bulbuls, and honeybees visit the habitat.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Plant seeds, water herbs, and fill clay bird bowls in a school garden quadrant.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Birds flutter in with cheerful chirp audio. A biodiversity species catalog logs each visiting bird and insect.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Attract 5 different bird and pollinator species to the garden oasis.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Unity in Diversity: Languages, Attire, and Terrains
interactives.interactive_title: Incredible India Cultural Tapestry & Language Explorer
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Appreciate India's pluralistic cultural heritage, regional traditional attire, and constitutional unity.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Meera explores how clothing and lifestyle adapt to geography: woollen pherans in Kashmir, cotton lungis in Kerala, and colorful turbans in Rajasthan. Students match traditional attire to state geographies.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click on states across India to dress avatar characters in authentic regional costumes and listen to greeting phrases in local languages.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Costumes render in rich textile detail. An audio greeting plays: 'Vanakkam', 'Namaskara', 'Sat Sri Akal', 'Khamma Ghani'.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Explore all 4 cultural regions of India (North, South, East, West).

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Harvest Festivals: Celebrating Nature's Bounty
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Recognize that major Indian festivals align with solar transitions, crop harvest, and gratitude to nature.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Farhan celebrates how Bihu in Assam, Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Makar Sankranti in Gujarat, and Baisakhi in Punjab all thank nature for fertile crops. Students match traditional festive foods and customs to regional harvest seasons.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Spin a seasonal calendar wheel to autumn, winter, and spring. Drag festival badges to their respective states.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Festive animations activate (Pongal pots boiling over, Bihu dancers with dhol, kites filling Gujarat skies).
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Correctly map 5 major harvest celebrations across India.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Traditional Handicrafts, Folk Art, and Architecture
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Analyze how indigenous dwellings use local materials optimized for regional weather.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Tenzing compares stone and slate houses in Ladakh with sloping red-tile roofs in Kerala and bamboo stilt homes in Assam. Students test how each house type responds to snow, heavy rain, or desert heat.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Select a home style and subject it to simulated extreme weather (Snowstorm, Torrential Monsoon, 45°C Heatwave).
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Houses matched to correct climates resist damage; mismatched houses fail (e.g. flat roofs collapse under heavy snow).
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Correctly match 4 indigenous house designs to their native climates.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Shanti's Travel Dream: Starting from the Southern Tip
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Map India's geographical span (~3,214 km) from Kanyakumari to Ladakh.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Shanti plans an expedition with Appa and Amma starting at Kanyakumari on the southern coast and journeying north through plains and high Himalayan passes to Ladakh.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drag the travel van along national highways. Stop at milestones to inspect changing terrains and climates.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Landscape panos morph from palm-lined coastal beaches to dry Deccan plateaus to towering snow-capped Himalayan ridges.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Complete the 3,200 km itinerary with all waypoints checked.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Kanyakumari: Triveni Sangam of Three Waters
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand the unique geography of Kanyakumari where three oceanic bodies meet.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Amma stands with Shanti on Kanyakumari beach where the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean meet. Students scrub daytime hours to watch the simultaneous sunset and full moonrise over the waters.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Rotate the sun/moon dial. Toggle labels showing the 3 distinct water bodies meeting at the peninsula tip.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: The sky changes colors; ocean waves intersect in rhythmic cross-swells at the confluence point.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Identify all 3 oceans and observe the full moon sunset alignment.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Ladakh: The High-Altitude Cold Desert & Nomads
interactives.interactive_title: Changpa Nomadic Camp & Rebo Tent Insulator
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Examine adaptations to high-altitude cold deserts, nomadic pastoralism, and yak-wool insulation.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: At 4,000 metres on the Changthang plateau, Shanti meets the Changpa nomads living in Rebo tents and grazing Pashmina goats. Students assemble a Rebo tent using woven yak-wool strips to test interior warmth.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Pitch a virtual Rebo tent with wooden poles and yak-wool cloth. Monitor indoor vs outdoor temperature during a -15°C blizzard.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Thick yak wool blocks freezing winds; interior hearth keeps temperature at comfortable +12°C. Pashmina goats graze on alpine tundra.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Maintain a warm shelter and protect the goat herd through a cold desert night.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: What Floats, What Sinks? Exploring Buoyancy
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Demonstrate that shape and water displacement determine whether an object floats or sinks.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Ayesha crumbles aluminum foil into a tight ball and it sinks; when shaped into a wide boat, it floats carrying small pebbles! Students test various objects (iron nail, foil boat, wooden block, coin) in a water tank.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Drop objects into a water tank. Drag edges of the foil to reshape it between a ball and a hollow boat.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Displaced water overflows into a measuring beaker. Buoyant force arrow (pointing UP) and Gravity arrow (pointing DOWN) visualize balance of forces.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Shape a piece of foil to carry 5 pebbles without sinking.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: The Salt Water Mystery: Floating an Egg
interactives.interactive_title: Salt Water Density & Buoyant Lift Lab
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Observe how dissolving solute increases liquid density and enhances upward buoyant force.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Hamid places a fresh egg in tap water; it sinks to the bottom. As Ayesha stirs spoons of common salt into the water, its density increases until the egg bobs to the surface.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click to add spoons of salt into a glass with an egg. Watch a stirrer dissolve the salt.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: A hydrometer gauge tracks liquid density from 1.00 g/cm³ up to 1.15 g/cm³. At 3 spoons, the egg floats triumphantly.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Find the minimum salt concentration required to float an egg and a lemon.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: The Dead Sea & Solar Salt Pans
interactives.interactive_title: Dead Sea Floating & Coastal Salt Pan Crystallizer
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand hyper-salinity and how table salt is harvested through solar evaporation in coastal pans.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: In the Dead Sea (300 g salt per litre), people float reading newspapers. In coastal salt pans, seawater evaporates under the hot sun to leave sparkling salt crystals.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Place a virtual swimmer into fresh water vs Dead Sea water. Adjust sun and wind sliders over a coastal salt pan.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Swimmer floats effortlessly on the surface. Salt pan water evaporates leaving crystallized edible salt grains.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Harvest 100 kg of pure sea salt through solar evaporation.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Nature's Master Weavers: Spiders and Birds
interactives.interactive_title: Spider Orb Web Geometric Construction Lab
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Explore biomimetic weaving in animal architectures: spider silk tensile strength and orb geometry.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: A garden spider spins an intricate orb web. Students guide the spider to anchor bridge threads, build radial spokes, and weave a sticky capture spiral with equal geometric spacing.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Click to spin bridge line, radial spokes, and concentric spiral loops across tree branches.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Silk threads stretch with elastic tension. Wind gusts test the web's aerodynamic strength.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Complete a full 16-spoke symmetrical spider web that captures flying insects.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: From Cotton Pod to Spun Yarn
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Sequence raw cotton processing: harvesting, ginning, carding, and spinning into yarn on a charkha.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Prashant removes seeds from fluffy cotton bolls (ginning), cards the tangled fibres straight, and spins them on a traditional charkha wheel into strong, uniform yarn.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Rotate the charkha wheel handle using a circular mouse drag. Maintain steady speed to prevent thread breakage.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Twisted yarn wraps onto the spindle. A tension dial warns if spun too fast or too slow. Thread length counter increments.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Spin 50 metres of continuous cotton yarn.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: The Handloom & Pochampally Weaves
interactives.interactive_title: Pochampally Ikat Handloom Pit Loom Simulator
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand warp and weft interlacing on handlooms and traditional tie-dyeing techniques.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Weaver Uncle operates a pit loom in Pochampally village. Students press foot treadles to lift alternating warp threads, throwing the shuttle through the shed to weave geometric silk motifs.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Press 'Left Treadle', click 'Throw Shuttle', press 'Right Treadle', pull 'Beater Reed'.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Authentic clack-clack sound effects. The Pochampally saree fabric grows row by row with diamond patterns.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Weave 20 rows of authentic Pochampally patterned fabric.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: India's Geographic Panoramas: Diverse Terrains
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Differentiate between mountains, river plains, peninsular plateaus, desert dunes, and coastal mangroves.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Sonam shows how India's topography varies dramatically. Students sculpt a 3D elevation map, raising the Himalayan ranges, carving the Gangetic plains, and shaping the Thar desert.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Raise, lower, and smooth terrain heights on an interactive 3D mesh map. Toggle satellite texture views.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Elevation color bands update (Dark green for plains 0-200m, brown for plateaus, white for snowy peaks >6,000m).
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Sculpt all 5 physiographic divisions of India accurately.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Mountain Living & Terrace Agriculture
interactives.interactive_title: Mountain Terrace Farming Soil Erosion Lab
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Model how carving step terraces prevents soil erosion and retains moisture on steep slopes.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: On steep Himalayan slopes, torrential rain washes topsoil away. Students carve horizontal steps into a mountainside, simulating heavy monsoon storms to compare soil erosion with an untreated plain slope.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Carve 1 to 5 terraces on a slope. Click 'Trigger Monsoon Storm' to release heavy rainwater.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: On untreated slopes, mud cascades down (severe erosion); on terraced steps, water pools gently and irrigates apple trees with zero soil loss.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Protect 95% of topsoil through optimal terrace engineering.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Desert & Coastal Adaptations: Mud Walls & Mangroves
interactives.interactive_title: Thermal Mud Wall Insulation & Mangrove Wave Buffer
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Analyze how thick earthen walls delay desert heat transfer and coastal mangrove root systems buffer storm surges.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Kamla shows how two-foot-thick mud walls keep desert rooms at 24°C while outside temperatures reach 48°C. Ramu shows how coastal mangrove root networks absorb 80% of storm wave energy.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Adjust wall thickness from 10 cm to 60 cm under 48°C desert sun. Test tidal wave impacts on bare coastline vs mangrove forest.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Thermal heat gradient shows slow heat penetration through thick mud walls. Wave height sensors show waves dissipate through mangrove roots.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Maintain a cool indoor shelter and defend a coastal village from storm surges.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Looking Down from Space: An Astronaut's Perspective
interactives.interactive_title: ISS Cupola Panoramic Orbital View with Shubhanshu Shukla
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Experience the Overview Effect: viewing Earth from space as one interconnected, borderless home.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla looks out of the International Space Station cupola window. He reflects: 'Earth looks completely one, no border is visible from outside.' Students look through the 7 panoramic windows of the ISS cupola at Earth rotating below.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Look around a 360° virtual ISS cupola window. Zoom in on continents, glowing city night lights, and cloud vortexes.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Real orbital speed of 28,000 km/h is simulated. National borders vanish, revealing mountain ranges, deserts, and vast blue oceans.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Complete 1 full 90-minute orbital revolution around Earth.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: The Fragile Blue Atmosphere & Microgravity
interactives.interactive_title: Atmospheric Ribbon Life Support & Microgravity Lab
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand how Earth's thin atmospheric blanket shields life from solar radiation and meteors.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Deepa notices the paper-thin glowing blue ribbon around Earth's limb. Students launch cosmic rays and meteors toward Earth to observe the atmosphere burning meteors as shooting stars and filtering ultraviolet rays.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Toggle atmospheric protection layers (Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere). Launch incoming space debris.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Meteors burn with glowing trails in the mesosphere. Radiation meters show safe levels on Earth's surface.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Demonstrate the 3 critical life-support functions of the atmosphere.

interactives.subject: Science EVS
interactives.lesson_title: Stewards of Spaceship Earth: Our Shared Future
interactives.pedagogical_objective: Understand planetary environmental stewardship and managing finite global resources.
interactives.book_faithful_explanation: Captain Shukla reminds us: 'Earth is our one home, and all of us are in it.' Students balance clean air, freshwater reserves, forest cover, and renewable energy on a global planetary dashboard.
interactives.user_interaction_mechanics: Adjust policy sliders: Reforestation, Renewable Energy, Water Conservation, Waste Reduction.
interactives.real_time_visuals_and_feedback: Earth's health index rises from critical yellow to radiant green. Global biodiversity and human well-being indices flourish.
interactives.success_criteria_and_rewards: Achieve 100% planetary sustainability equilibrium.
